droid-monkey attacked this Android app with a real-world fault and it failed. Fix the root cause.

## What happened
Attack `permission_revoke` (permission_revoke): Grant a permission through the app, revoke it the way Settings does, come back and use the feature again.
Steps: [{"tap": "scan_coupon"}, {"accept_permission": true}, {"settle": 3}, {"fault": "revoke_permission", "permission": "android.permission.CAMERA"}, {"restart_to_screen": true}, {"tap": "scan_coupon"}, {"settle": 4.0}]
Result: crashed: java.lang.SecurityException: validateClientPermissionsLocked:1848: Caller "com.shubhasai.monkeymart" (PID 11563, UID 10236) cannot open camera "1" without camera permission
Crash: java.lang.SecurityException @ com.shubhasai.monkeymart.ui.CouponScanner.open(CouponScanner.kt:44)
  at com.shubhasai.monkeymart.ui.CouponScanner.open(CouponScanner.kt:44)
  at com.shubhasai.monkeymart.ui.CouponScannerKt.ScanCouponButton$lambda$9$lambda$8$lambda$7(CouponScanner.kt:77)
  at com.shubhasai.monkeymart.ui.CouponScannerKt$$ExternalSyntheticLambda2.invoke(D8$$SyntheticClass:0)

## Diagnosis
Root cause: The coupon scanner decides whether it may open the camera from a persisted SharedPreferences flag, `camera_granted`, that is set to true once and never cleared (CouponScanner.kt:33-38). The button's onClick at CouponScanner.kt:76-77 trusts that flag and calls `CouponScanner.open` directly, which calls `CameraManager.openCamera` at line 44 with no permission check. When the user revokes CAMERA in Settings, the process restarts, the stale flag still says true, and the open call throws SecurityException. The design error is caching a runtime permission state instead of asking the system at the moment of use.
Fix approach: Drop the SharedPreferences flag. In the onClick, check `ContextCompat.checkSelfPermission(context, CAMERA)` at use time and only call `open` when it returns GRANTED; otherwise launch the permission request. Also wrap the `openCamera` call in a try/catch for SecurityException and surface a status message, so a revocation that happens between the check and the open does not crash the app.
Evidence: app/src/main/java/com/shubhasai/monkeymart/ui/CouponScanner.kt:31-38 - the 'camera_granted' SharedPreferences flag is written to true on grant and read back as the access check; nothing clears it or re-checks the live permission; app/src/main/java/com/shubhasai/monkeymart/ui/CouponScanner.kt:76-77 - onClick opens the camera whenever the cached flag is true, without checking the permission; app/src/main/java/com/shubhasai/monkeymart/ui/CouponScanner.kt:43-44 - cameraIdList and openCamera run with no permission check; this is where the SecurityException is thrown after revocation; app/src/main/java/com/shubhasai/monkeymart/ui/CouponScanner.kt:64-67 - the only place the flag is set, in the permission-result callback, so it is never reset when the permission is later revoked; app/src/main/java/com/shubhasai/monkeymart/ui/CheckoutScreen.kt:74 - ScanCouponButton is the only entry point to the scanner on the checkout form

## Files to change
- app/src/main/java/com/shubhasai/monkeymart/ui/CouponScanner.kt

## Regression test
Add an instrumented test in src/androidTest, CouponScannerPermissionTest. Grant CAMERA, open checkout, tap scan_coupon, then revoke CAMERA with `pm revoke` (or UiAutomation.revokeRuntimePermission) and restart the activity. Tap scan_coupon again and assert the app does not crash and that the coupon_status text shows the permission prompt or a camera-permission message instead of the scanner. Before the fix this test crashes with SecurityException at CouponScanner.kt:44; after the fix it passes.

## Rules
- Fix the root cause in the files above with the idiomatic Android approach. Keep the change small and focused.
- Add exactly one regression test file under app/src/test (JVM unit test, preferred) or app/src/androidTest
  (instrumented), using only test libraries the project already has (see app/build.gradle.kts). It must fail on
  the old code and pass on the fixed code.
- Do not change build files or add dependencies. Do not touch unrelated code. Do not commit.
- When done, reply with one short paragraph: what you changed and the test class name.

addedLines: - claude: Catch-all for any task that doesn't fit a more specific agent. FleetView's default when no agent name is typed. (Tools: *)

- claude-code-guide: Use this agent when the user asks questions ("Can Claude...", "Does Claude...", "How do I...") about: (1) Claude Code (the CLI tool) - features, hooks, slash commands, MCP servers, settings, IDE integrations, keyboard shortcuts; (2) Claude Agent SDK - building custom agents; (3) Claude API (formerly Anthropic API) - API usage, tool use, Anthropic SDK usage. **IMPORTANT:** Before spawning a new agent, check if there is already a running or recently completed claude-code-guide agent that you can continue via SendMessage. (Tools: Bash, Read, WebFetch, WebSearch)

- Explore: Fast read-only search agent for locating code. Use it to find files by pattern (eg. "src/components/**/*.tsx"), grep for symbols or keywords (eg. "API endpoints"), or answer "where is X defined / which files reference Y." Do NOT use it for code review, design-doc auditing, cross-file consistency checks, or open-ended analysis — it reads excerpts rather than whole files and will miss content past its read window. When calling, specify search breadth: "quick" for a single targeted lookup, "medium" for moderate exploration, or "very thorough" to search across multiple locations and naming conventions. (Tools: All tools except Agent, ExitPlanMode, Edit, Write, NotebookEdit)

- general-purpose: General-purpose agent for researching complex questions, searching for code, and executing multi-step tasks. When you are searching for a keyword or file and are not confident that you will find the right match in the first few tries use this agent to perform the search for you. (Tools: *)

- Plan: Software architect agent for designing implementation plans. Use this when you need to plan the implementation strategy for a task. Returns step-by-step plans, identifies critical files, and considers architectural trade-offs. (Tools: All tools except Agent, ExitPlanMode, Edit, Write, NotebookEdit)
- statusline-setup: Use this agent to configure the user's Claude Code status line setting. (Tools: Read, Edit)

- update-config: Use this skill to configure the Claude Code harness via settings.json. Automated behaviors ("from now on when X", "each time X", "whenever X", "before/after X") require hooks configured in settings.json - the harness executes these, not Claude, so memory/preferences cannot fulfill them. Also use for: permissions ("allow X", "add permission", "move permission to"), env vars ("set X=Y"), hook troubleshooting, or any changes to settings.json/settings.local.json files. Examples: "allow npm commands", "add bq permission to global settings", "move permission to user settings", "set DEBUG=true", "when claude stops show X". For simple settings like theme/model, suggest the /config command.
- keybindings-help: Use when the user wants to customize keyboard shortcuts, rebind keys, add chord bindings, or modify ~/.claude/keybindings.json. Examples: "rebind ctrl+s", "add a chord shortcut", "change the submit key", "customize keybindings".
- simplify: Review changed code for reuse, quality, and efficiency, then fix any issues found.
- fewer-permission-prompts: Scan your transcripts for common read-only Bash and MCP tool calls, then add a prioritized allowlist to project .claude/settings.json to reduce permission prompts.
- loop: Run a prompt or slash command on a recurring interval (e.g. /loop 5m /foo). Omit the interval to let the model self-pace. - When the user wants to set up a recurring task, poll for status, or run something repeatedly on an interval (e.g. "check the deploy every 5 minutes", "keep running /babysit-prs"). Do NOT invoke for one-off tasks.
- schedule: Create, update, list, or run scheduled remote agents (routines) that execute on a cron schedule. - When the user wants to schedule a recurring remote agent, set up automated tasks, create a cron job for Claude Code, or manage their scheduled agents/routines. Also use when the user wants a one-time scheduled run ("run this once at 3pm", "remind me to check X tomorrow").
- claude-api: Build, debug, and optimize Claude API / Anthropic SDK apps. Apps built with this skill should include prompt caching. Also handles migrating existing Claude API code between Claude model versions (4.5 → 4.6, 4.6 → 4.7, retired-model replacements).
TRIGGER when: code imports `anthropic`/`@anthropic-ai/sdk`; user asks for the Claude API, Anthropic SDK, or Managed Agents; user adds/modifies/tunes a Claude feature (caching, thinking, compaction, tool use, batch, files, citations, memory) or model (Opus/Sonnet/Haiku) in a file; questions about prompt caching / cache hit rate in an Anthropic SDK project.
SKIP: file imports `openai`/other-provider SDK, filename like `*-openai.py`/`*-generic.py`, provider-neutral code, general programming/ML.
- init: Initialize a new CLAUDE.md file with codebase documentation
- review: Review a pull request
- security-review: Complete a security review of the pending changes on the current branch

A docs skill your client lists → load it before any docs call — also before a `read`, comment or tab change on a claude.ai …/artifact/… link (the link is a doc; never web-fetch it). If the permission is lost between the check and the open, the app shows "Camera permission is needed to scan coupons" instead of crashing.
- **Test:** `CouponScannerPermissionTest` is an instrumented test. It plants the stale `camera_granted=true` flag, opens checkout and taps `scan_coupon`. It then asserts there's no crash and that `coupon_status` doesn't say "Scanner ready".
